# wasm_harness_server

Runs the official craftinginterpreters Lox test suite (`rox/mothership/test/**/*.lox`)
against the Wasm build of `rox/library`, from Node.

## Setup

1. Build the library for Node (this is a separate `wasm-pack` target from
   whatever you use for an in-browser demo page):

   ```sh
   cd ../library
   wasm-pack build --target nodejs --out-dir pkg
   ```

   `--target nodejs` is required: it produces a synchronous CommonJS module
   that this app can `require`/`import` directly, unlike `--target web`,
   which needs an async `init()` call meant for browsers.

2. Install this app's dependencies:

   ```sh
   cd ../wasm_harness_server
   npm install
   ```

## Running

Development (no build step, uses `tsx`):

```sh
npm run test:dev
```

Compiled:

```sh
npm run build
npm test
```

Exit code is `0` if every test passed, `1` if anything failed.

## Adjusting for your VM's coverage

`src/discover.ts` excludes `test/benchmark`, `test/scanning`, and
`test/expressions` by default, since those target performance measurement or
earlier, non-bytecode chapters of the book. Edit `DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_DIRS`
there if your port's coverage differs.

## Notes on fidelity to the official test runner

`src/parser.ts` reimplements the `// expect: ...` / `// expect runtime
error: ...` / `// [line N] Error ...` comment conventions used by the
official Dart test runner (`tool/bin/test.dart` in the
`munificent/craftinginterpreters` repository), based on the documented
convention. It is not a verified line-for-line port of that Dart source. If
a specific test behaves unexpectedly, compare its comments against
`tool/bin/test.dart` directly.
